title: Audit selected-SDK host audio stream and headless device contracts
goal: Investigate actual selected-SDK host stream ownership, bounded queues/callbacks and SDL dummy-device lifecycle with original PCM, before title playback is available; retain demonstrated failures and a repair handoff without changing shared SDK or guest services.
acceptance: Execute the actual dynamically loaded approved audio system and selected SDL audio provider where requested, binding exact package, compiler, configuration and loaded-library hashes; do not substitute audio implementations or manufacture device success

Exercise original PCM through bounded stream capacity, invalid/closed/reopened stream identities, queue limits, played-callback ownership, underrun counters, close/reopen and repeated shutdown; use silent timer and real SDL dummy-device configurations explicitly distinguished

Require fresh-process completion, unchanged other-stream counters, resource recovery and meaningful wrong-result/incomplete-process controls; retain any SDK contract failures instead of weakening expectations or silently repairing shared code

Keep private profiles/output/process handles isolated and changes within this diagnostic lane; no guest service admission, proprietary codec/save input, audible/title playback certification, physical device loss claim or shared SDK/interface edit
validation: Run isolated, repeated and reordered original cases on Windows/Linux using supported host sanitizers and exact approved native SDK packages; record uninstrumented SDK coverage and unavailable backend/hardware checks explicitly
Validate result/package/library identities against duplicate, stale, wrong-case, malformed, partial and wrong-output controls; crash/timeouts cannot pass ordinary cases

Measure original host submission/callback/lifecycle costs over at least three independent processes, retaining failures and timing limits; run public checks and publish actionable separate repair/integration prerequisites without marking MW3-082 or any gameplay/audio gate complete
size: bounded game-free selected-SDK audio investigation; title/device/SDK repairs stay separate
evidence: docs/engine/sdk-audio.md; original tests/host_platform/sdk_audio and tools/test_sdk_audio.py execute actual approved rexapu and SDL3 provider modules with private PCM/configuration and exact loaded audio/provider/SDL/app/base identities

Four native/host-sanitizer profiles on Windows/Linux retain 132 process outcomes: 92 PASS including 20 expected controls, 40 real lifetime-ownership FAIL, no runtime skips. All four suites correctly exit 1; investigation completion is not passing stream ownership or title audio

A closed stream is rejected before reuse, but its replacement reuses raw ID 2; submitting through the old ID succeeds and invokes the replacement callback. Other stream/old callback counts stay unchanged. Three isolated runs and both case orders reproduce this in every mode/profile; no SDK or interface repair is hidden

Eight-stream bounds, invalid/closed IDs before reuse, four-frame queue refusal/drain, independent callbacks, underruns and 32 close/observer cycles pass. Each lifecycle case opens 64 streams and accepts 160 frames; streams/queues, SDK-tracked threads and SDL audio state recover. This is not a general OS/SDK leak or mixed-sample correctness claim

Strict nonce/mode/case/typed completion and library guards pass 11 Python tests, including an actual owned-child timeout with plausible output. Wrong-result, incomplete-record and invalid-backend controls pass after retaining newline/category/shutdown fixture errors and one deliberately forced-exit Windows control crash; that crash is not normal shutdown success or repaired SDK behavior

Windows host UBSan traps and Linux host ASan/UBSan exercise identical native SDK bytes; audio/SDL library internals remain uninstrumented. Source/driver/binary/library/log/artifact identities are rehashed and exact receipts published as hashes only

Three independent native lifecycle runs per mode measure 160 accepted Submit calls each: per-run medians 0.700-1.000 us Windows and 0.507-0.595 us Linux, with raw tails and callback-progress elapsed times retained. Synthetic one-host costs only; no audible latency, title playback, codec fidelity or fastest-framework claim

Public Windows Release check.py passes 177 Python tests/eight skips plus parser CTest 1/1; Linux Release --sanitizers passes 177 tests/two Windows-only skips plus parser 1/1. Self-review only; owner-token/SDK interface/guest admission and MW3-082 audible/physical-device checks require separate agreed work. No game bytes, SDK, private traces or shared input/startup/allocation/runtime/CI files committed
